+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+
+import pytest
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware import freebsd, openbsd, netbsd, darwin
+
+
+class UptimeModule(object):
+    def __init__(self, result=(0, '100\n', ''), path='/sbin/sysctl'):
+        self.result = result
+        self.path = path
+        self.commands = []
+
+    def get_bin_path(self, name):
+        return self.path
+
+    def run_command(self, command):
+        self.commands.append(command)
+        return self.result
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('hardware_class', [
+    freebsd.FreeBSDHardware, openbsd.OpenBSDHardware,
+    netbsd.NetBSDHardware, darwin.DarwinHardware,
+])
+def test_bsd_uptime_uses_numeric_boot_time(hardware_class, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr('time.time', lambda: 150.9)
+    module = UptimeModule()
+    assert hardware_class(module).get_uptime_facts() == {'uptime_seconds': 50}
+    assert module.commands == [['/sbin/sysctl', '-n', 'kern.boottime']]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('output', ['', ' ', 'not-a-number', '{ sec = 100, usec = 0 }'])
+def test_bsd_uptime_omits_invalid_boot_time(output):
+    module = UptimeModule((0, output, ''))
+    assert freebsd.FreeBSDHardware(module).get_uptime_facts() == {}
+
+
+def test_bsd_uptime_omits_failed_command():
+    module = UptimeModule((1, '', 'failed'))
+    assert freebsd.FreeBSDHardware(module).get_uptime_facts() == {}
+
+
+def test_bsd_uptime_missing_sysctl_raises_value_error():
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        freebsd.FreeBSDHardware(UptimeModule(path=None)).get_uptime_facts()
+
+
+def test_freebsd_populate_includes_uptime_with_other_hardware(monkeypatch):
+    module = UptimeModule()
+    monkeypatch.setattr('time.time', lambda: 150)
+    hardware = freebsd.FreeBSDHardware(module)
+    for method, facts in [('get_cpu_facts', {'processor_count': 2}),
+                          ('get_memory_facts', {'memtotal_mb': 1024}),
+                          ('get_dmi_facts', {'system_vendor': 'Example'}),
+                          ('get_device_facts', {'devices': []}),
+                          ('get_mount_facts', {'mounts': []})]:
+        monkeypatch.setattr(hardware, method, lambda facts=facts: facts)
+    assert hardware.populate() == {'processor_count': 2, 'memtotal_mb': 1024,
+                                   'system_vendor': 'Example', 'devices': [],
+                                   'mounts': [], 'uptime_seconds': 50}
+
+
+def test_openbsd_populate_keeps_other_facts_when_sysctl_has_bad_line(monkeypatch):
+    class OpenBSDModule(UptimeModule):
+        def __init__(self):
+            super(OpenBSDModule, self).__init__()
+            self.warnings = []
+
+        def run_command(self, command):
+            if command == ['/sbin/sysctl', 'hw', 'kern']:
+                return (0, 'hw.ncpu: 2\nbad-line\nhw.model: CPU\nhw.disknames: sd0\n', '')
+            return super(OpenBSDModule, self).run_command(command)
+
+        def warn(self, message):
+            self.warnings.append(message)
+
+    module = OpenBSDModule()
+    hardware = openbsd.OpenBSDHardware(module)
+    monkeypatch.setattr('time.time', lambda: 150)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(hardware, 'get_memory_facts', lambda: {'memtotal_mb': 1024})
+    monkeypatch.setattr(hardware, 'get_mount_facts', lambda: {'mounts': []})
+    facts = hardware.populate()
+    assert facts['uptime_seconds'] == 50
+    assert facts['processor_count'] == '2'
+    assert facts['memtotal_mb'] == 1024
+    assert facts['devices'] == ['sd0']
+    assert facts['mounts'] == []
+    assert len(module.warnings) == 1
+    assert module.warnings[0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (bad-line): ')
diff --git a/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py b/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b33b26b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py
@@ -0,0 +1,69 @@
+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+
+import pytest
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl import get_sysctl
+
+
+class SysctlModule(object):
+    def __init__(self, result=(0, '', ''), error=None, path='/sbin/sysctl'):
+        self.result = result
+        self.error = error
+        self.path = path
+        self.warnings = []
+        self.commands = []
+
+    def get_bin_path(self, name):
+        return self.path
+
+    def run_command(self, command):
+        self.commands.append(command)
+        if self.error:
+            raise self.error
+        return self.result
+
+    def warn(self, message):
+        self.warnings.append(message)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('output, expected', [
+    ('hw.ncpu=4\nkern.osrelease: 7.5\nvm.swappiness = 60\n',
+     {'hw.ncpu': '4', 'kern.osrelease': '7.5', 'vm.swappiness': '60'}),
+    ('hw.ncpu 4\nkern.osrelease: 7.5\n',
+     {'hw.ncpu': '4', 'kern.osrelease': '7.5'}),
+    ('hw.model: first line\n    second line\n\tthird line\nhw.ncpu: 4\n',
+     {'hw.model': 'first line\n    second line\n\tthird line', 'hw.ncpu': '4'}),
+])
+def test_get_sysctl_parses_platform_delimiters_and_continuations(output, expected):
+    module = SysctlModule((0, output, ''))
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == expected
+    assert module.commands == [['/sbin/sysctl', 'hw']]
+
+
+def test_get_sysctl_keeps_valid_lines_after_malformed_line():
+    module = SysctlModule((0, 'hw.ncpu: 4\nmalformed\nhw.model: CPU\n', ''))
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {'hw.ncpu': '4', 'hw.model': 'CPU'}
+    assert len(module.warnings) == 1
+    assert module.warnings[0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (malformed): ')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('result, error, message', [
+    ((1, '', 'permission denied'), None, 'permission denied'),
+    (None, OSError('no device'), 'no device'),
+    (None, IOError('read error'), 'read error'),
+])
+def test_get_sysctl_warns_and_returns_empty_on_command_failure(result, error, message):
+    module = SysctlModule(result, error)
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    assert module.warnings == ['Unable to read sysctl: ' + message]
+
+
+def test_get_sysctl_warns_when_binary_lookup_fails():
+    module = SysctlModule()
+
+    def missing_binary(name):
+        raise OSError('lookup failed')
+
+    module.get_bin_path = missing_binary
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    assert module.warnings == ['Unable to read sysctl: lookup failed']

+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+
+import pytest
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl import get_sysctl
+
+
+class SysctlModule(object):
+    def __init__(self, result=(0, '', ''), error=None, path='/sbin/sysctl'):
+        self.result = result
+        self.error = error
+        self.path = path
+        self.warnings = []
+        self.commands = []
+
+    def get_bin_path(self, name):
+        return self.path
+
+    def run_command(self, command):
+        self.commands.append(command)
+        if self.error:
+            raise self.error
+        return self.result
+
+    def warn(self, message):
+        self.warnings.append(message)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('output, expected', [
+    ('hw.ncpu=4\nkern.osrelease: 7.5\nvm.swappiness = 60\n',
+     {'hw.ncpu': '4', 'kern.osrelease': '7.5', 'vm.swappiness': '60'}),
+    ('hw.ncpu 4\nkern.osrelease: 7.5\n',
+     {'hw.ncpu': '4', 'kern.osrelease': '7.5'}),
+    ('hw.model: first line\n    second line\n\tthird line\nhw.ncpu: 4\n',
+     {'hw.model': 'first line\n    second line\n\tthird line', 'hw.ncpu': '4'}),
+])
+def test_get_sysctl_parses_platform_delimiters_and_continuations(output, expected):
+    module = SysctlModule((0, output, ''))
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == expected
+    assert module.commands == [['/sbin/sysctl', 'hw']]
+
+
+def test_get_sysctl_keeps_valid_lines_after_malformed_line():
+    module = SysctlModule((0, 'hw.ncpu: 4\nmalformed\nhw.model: CPU\n', ''))
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {'hw.ncpu': '4', 'hw.model': 'CPU'}
+    assert len(module.warnings) == 1
+    assert module.warnings[0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (malformed): ')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('result, error, message', [
+    ((1, '', 'permission denied'), None, 'permission denied'),
+    (None, OSError('no device'), 'no device'),
+    (None, IOError('read error'), 'read error'),
+])
+def test_get_sysctl_warns_and_returns_empty_on_command_failure(result, error, message):
+    module = SysctlModule(result, error)
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    assert module.warnings == ['Unable to read sysctl: ' + message]
+
+
+def test_get_sysctl_warns_when_binary_lookup_fails():
+    module = SysctlModule()
+
+    def missing_binary(name):
+        raise OSError('lookup failed')
+
+    module.get_bin_path = missing_binary
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    assert module.warnings == ['Unable to read sysctl: lookup failed']
